newsitem.title: USA: New treatments offer hope to lung cancer patients.
newsitem.headline: New treatments offer hope to lung cancer patients.

text.p: New treatments for lung cancer, one of which involves injecting genetic material directly into tumours, have lengthened the lives of some patients, a researcher said on Tuesday.

In the past, lung cancer killed nine out of 10 patients within one year, but a variety of new drug treatments have lifted one-year survival rates to between 35 percent and 50 percent and improved quality of life as well, Chandra Belani of the University of Pittsburgh Cancer Institute said.
In some cases, chemotherapy combined with radiation treatments have allowed up to half of the patients to live two to three years, he said.

A revolutionary approach to the deadly disease was being tried where the p53 gene that is missing or altered in half of patients was injected directly into the tumour to try to reverse the cancer development.
Belani presented his findings along with other cancer experts at a news conference organised by the Journal of American Medical Association.

The American Cancer Society estimated that 178,000 new cases of lung cancer would be diagnosed this year and there will be more than 160,000 lung cancer-related deaths. Smokers were at 10 times the risk of developing the disease.
Belani said screening for lung cancer had yet to make a difference in overall survival rates, and that the symptoms were difficult to discern.
